Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` checks that a zip entry with complex permission settings (with more than one flag set) should not be incorrectly detected as a Unix symlink. The current bug report mentions that entries with Unix permission mode 177777 incorrectly return true for `isUnixSymlink`.

Investigating the `isUnixSymlink()` method of `ZipArchiveEntry`, it returns true if the Unix permission bits of the entry have only the symbolic link flag set, i.e., it checks:

```java
return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
```

Looking at `getUnixMode()`, it extracts the Unix mode bits from `externalAttributes` only if the entry platform is Unix. It shifts right and masks to get a 16-bit mode.

The constant `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` corresponds to the octal value `0120000` (symbolic link bit in Unix stat).

The bug arises because `isUnixSymlink()` only checks if the link flag bit is set in the mode, but does not ensure that *only* that flag is set. Hence, if other bits are set alongside the symlink flag (for example `177777` which is a complex permission mask), the expression still evaluates to true because the link flag bit is present.

The test expects `isUnixSymlink()` to return false if more than one flag is set, but the method currently returns true if the link flag bit is just present regardless of other bits.

Thus, the root cause is a logic error in `isUnixSymlink()` which should verify that the mode exactly matches the `LINK_FLAG` bits (and no other bits are set), instead of merely testing if the link bit is set.

Recent bug reports about archiver or compressor extensions are unrelated here.

This matches the reported issue where entries with Unix mode `177777` (multiple bits) incorrectly report as symlinks. The fix is to tighten the check to confirm exclusive presence of the link flag bit in `isUnixSymlink()`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
